status_legend.needs review: Published here and does not block the release. A human should read it before buying.
status_legend.blocking: There are no blocking items: unverified values were left blank instead.

items.title: Only 4 of 43 listings use the words “solid gold”
items.affected: 39 of 43 rows (all except mej-deb, mej-db, mej-bde, mej-2mm)
items.finding: Four Mejuri listings quote “14k solid gold” in their own product text. The other 39 listings — all of Ross-Simons, Blue Nile, Brilliant Earth, Anna Sheffield, With Clarity and the Aurate rings — state a karat without ever using the word solid. None of the 39 carries plating language either, so they are probably solid alloys, but “probably” is exactly what your checklist says not to accept. The Aurate cigar band even sells a vermeil variant on the same page, which shows why the distinction matters.
items.buyer_action: Before paying, get the seller to confirm in writing: "solid 14K gold, not plated, not vermeil, not gold-filled, not gold over silver". Keep that message with the receipt.

items.title: Metal weight is published for 7 of 43 listings - the rest still cannot be value-checked
items.finding: The earlier passes recorded 1 of 43 as weight-published. Pass P12 found that this was wrong: Ross-Simons prints a 'Gold Weight' figure in the Details table of its product pages, and it reads 1.7 g (571221), 2.5 g (571222), 3.8 g (571223), 5.0 g (571213), 0.5 g (981367) and 0.5 g (907250). Aurate publishes a 2.6-4 g range for the Modern Cigar Band. That is 7 of 43 rows where the price can be compared with the gold actually in the ring. The other 36 - every Mejuri, Blue Nile, Brilliant Earth, With Clarity and Anna Sheffield row, plus 11 Ross-Simons rows - do not publish grams on the page read, so their cells stay blank rather than estimated.
items.buyer_action: For the 36 rows without a published weight, ask the seller for the gram weight of your exact size in writing and run the calculator with it. For the 7 rows with a weight, treat the figure as the seller's claim until an independent jeweller weighs the ring.

items.title: Aurate mixes vermeil and solid gold inside one listing
items.finding: The Modern Cigar Band feed reports price_min 118.00 and price_max 1668.00. 118.00 is the vermeil variant; the 14K variant is 1,308.00. A shopper who sorts by lowest price sees a vermeil price for a solid-gold product page.
items.buyer_action: Always switch the metal selector to 14K or 18K and re-read the price before adding to cart.

items.title: With Clarity prices are for the setting only
items.finding: These products carry the tag "Ring Setting Product". The listed range buys the metal setting; the centre diamond is a separate purchase. The total cost of a finished ring is therefore higher than the number shown.
items.buyer_action: Build the full ring (setting + stone) and compare the total, not the setting price.

items.title: Ross-Simons also sells a setting with the stone excluded
items.finding: The listing text states "Center stone and setting are sold separately." and the product is tagged SEMIMOUNTING. 1,269.00-1,439.00 does not buy a complete ring.
items.buyer_action: Read the phrase "setting" carefully; budget separately for the centre stone.

items.title: Two very low solid-gold prices — now testable against published weights
items.finding: $149 for a 14K ring and $179 for an 18K ring looked implausible. Pass P12 found both pages publish a metal weight: 0.5 grams each. At 14K that is about 0.29 g of fine gold; at 18K about 0.375 g. The prices are therefore consistent with extremely light rings, not with a mis-stated karat. The earlier finding said the value could not be checked; it now can, and the answer is "thin and light", not "fake".
items.buyer_action: Decide whether 0.5 g of metal is enough ring for daily wear. Weigh it on arrival - an independent jeweller can do this in a minute - and treat any shortfall from the stated 0.5 g as a return reason.

items.title: Estate pieces are one-of-a-kind and fixed size
items.finding: All three Ross-Simons estate listings are single-size, one-of-a-kind pieces. Ross-Simons' published policy refuses returns on merchandise 'altered, or resized by a jeweler other than Ross-Simons', so resizing can end your return right. The policy page retrieved does not publish a separate estate-jewellery carve-out either way, so estate-specific terms remain unconfirmed.
items.buyer_action: Buy your exact size, or have the retailer resize it. Get the return position in writing before ordering.

items.title: With Clarity Gerbera: is the sapphire included?
items.finding: The product is tagged "Ring Setting Product" (which normally means stone excluded) yet the description presents the marquise created sapphire as part of the ring. The listing does not resolve the contradiction.
items.buyer_action: Ask customer service, in writing, whether 1,210.00 includes the created sapphire centre stone.

items.title: Anna Sheffield price range is not explained line by line
items.finding: Bea Three Stone is listed 5,400.00-25,100.00 and Hazeline 7,150.00-9,200.00. The listings mention stone sizes but do not map each price to a specific configuration.
items.buyer_action: Ask for a written quote for the exact stone you are buying before paying.

items.title: No phone or support address verified for With Clarity
items.finding: Contact details were confirmed from official pages for Ross-Simons (phone 800-835-0919 and a support email), Aurate (support email) and Anna Sheffield (info@annasheffield.com). For With Clarity only official store metadata (Long Island City, NY, USD, ship-to countries) was confirmed; no phone number or support address was verified in this pass.
items.buyer_action: Find a phone number or postal address on With Clarity's own site and test it before ordering.

items.title: Return windows are short and returns are not free everywhere
items.finding: Anna Sheffield allows two weeks from delivery and charges a 10% restocking fee (capped at $500) on refunds. With Clarity allows 30 days but charges $250 if the diamond certificate is missing and $300 to re-certify. With Clarity also refuses returns on jewellery 'worked on, resized or repaired by another jeweler', and Anna Sheffield makes engraved or bespoke orders final sale. A return is therefore not automatically free or unlimited.
items.buyer_action: Decide within the window, keep every certificate and the original box, do not resize before you commit, and photograph the ring the day it arrives.

items.title: A hallmark and maker’s mark cannot be verified online
items.finding: No retailer page retrieved — in this pass or the first one — states the exact hallmark or maker’s mark that will be struck inside the band. A photograph of the inside of the band is the only pre-purchase evidence, and it still does not prove purity. US marking rules are set out in 16 CFR Part 23, including § 23.3 on misrepresentation of gold content and § 23.10 on quality marks.
items.buyer_action: Ask for a close-up photo of the stamp. On arrival, have an independent jeweller confirm the stamp and test purity (XRF preferred).

items.title: Aurate metal-variant prices are not mapped one-to-one
items.finding: For these three rings the feed reports only a min/max across 14K, 18K, platinum and ring sizes. The lowest price is not proven to be the 14K price, so the low end is shown as a range rather than as a 14K price.
items.buyer_action: Set metal to 14K and the size you need, then read the actual price before buying.

items.title: Carat weight is not the same as metal weight
items.finding: Listings quote ct. t.w. (total carat weight of stones). That says nothing about how many grams of gold you are buying, which is what the gold-value comparison needs. 16 CFR 23.18 covers misrepresentation of weight and "total weight".
items.buyer_action: Ask separately for the gold weight in grams. Keep stone weight and metal weight in separate columns, as this site does.

items.title: Blue Nile 18K ring description contradicts its own metal specification
items.finding: The Petite Nouveau Six-Prong Solitaire page is titled and specified as 18K Yellow Gold, but the product description on the same page says the ring is “crafted in polished 14k white gold”. One of the two statements is wrong. Do not buy without written confirmation of the metal from the seller.
items.buyer_action: Ask Blue Nile, in writing, which metal the 18K ring is and get it on the receipt. Photograph the stamp on arrival.

items.title: Search-engine snippet price ($925) does not match the live page ($1,420)
items.finding: A search result for Blue Nile item 203268 displayed “$925 (Setting Price)”. The live page read $1,420 on 2026-10-22. The live page is authoritative and is what this dataset records. This is why snippets are never used as price evidence in this project.
items.buyer_action: Never trust a search-result price. Open the live page and use that number, as this site does.

items.title: Mejuri Bold Diamond Eternity Ring: snippet $2,800 vs live $2,900
items.finding: A search snippet showed $2,800; the live page on the 14k white gold / natural diamond selection showed “From $2,900”. Mejuri prices vary by material, stone and size, and “From” prices move with size. The dataset records the material- and date-stamped value.
items.buyer_action: Set the exact metal, stone and size, then read the price. "From" prices are not purchase prices.

items.title: No listing in this pass publishes the ring's weight in grams (0 of 13)
items.finding: Gram weight is the single number needed to compare price against gold value. Blue Nile, Mejuri and Brilliant Earth pages publish width and thickness but not weight. Until a seller supplies weight in writing, the gold-value calculator cannot be applied to any row here. Ask the seller for the weight in grams before paying. SUPERSEDED by F02: pass P12 found that Ross-Simons does publish gold weight on six of the listings in this dataset, so '0 of 13' described the first pass's reading, not the seller's page.
items.buyer_action: Ask for the gram weight before paying, in writing. A jeweller can weigh it in seconds on arrival.

items.title: No listing publishes hallmark or maker's mark details (0 of 13)
items.finding: None of the pages reviewed state what is stamped inside the band. Under the National Stamping Act a quality mark must be accompanied by the maker's trademark, so the absence of published hallmark information is a legitimate pre-purchase question, not proof of a problem. Verify the stamp in person and with XRF after delivery.
items.buyer_action: Ask for a close-up photo of the inside of the band and have an independent jeweller read the stamp.

items.title: Setting-only prices are not ring prices (9 of 13 rows)
items.finding: Blue Nile and Brilliant Earth quote “Setting Price” / “Setting Only”, which excludes the centre diamond. A $1,000 setting plus a diamond is a materially different purchase. Mejuri's 4 rows are complete-ring prices, so the two groups must never be compared directly.
items.buyer_action: Budget for the centre stone separately; compare finished-ring totals, not setting prices.

items.title: “From” prices on Mejuri change with ring size
items.finding: Two Mejuri rows show “From $…”, meaning the selected size determines the final price. The recorded number is the lowest displayed price on the date checked.
items.buyer_action: Never budget from a "from" price. Configure the ring and re-read the total.

items.title: Blue Nile return window not confirmed on the pages read
items.finding: The product pages show a “Free Returns” badge and link to a Returns Policy, but do not state the number of days. The specific policy page was not opened in this pass, so the window and any resizing/custom exclusions are unverified.
items.buyer_action: Get the return window and any resize exclusion in writing before ordering.

items.title: Brilliant Earth return window not confirmed on the page read
items.finding: The page shows “Free Shipping & Returns” and “Free 1-Year Resizing”, but not the return window or exclusions. The dedicated returns page was not opened in this pass.
items.buyer_action: Get the return window in writing before ordering.

items.title: Independent reputation research not performed in this pass
items.finding: No BBB profile, state consumer-protection complaint record or independent review corpus was read for any of the three retailers. Contact information was verified (phone or store locator), but seller reputation is not yet independently verified for any retailer in this dataset.
items.buyer_action: Search the retailer name plus "complaints" on your own, and check the business address is real.

items.title: Regulatory text confirmed via official excerpts, not full section reads
items.finding: 16 CFR Part 23 was confirmed through the official eCFR index entry and the Federal Register final-rule text (including Note 2 to §23.10 and §23.4). Sections were not read in full, and a guessed FTC business-guidance URL returned 404.
items.buyer_action: Read the regulation section yourself before relying on it.

items.title: Credit-card purchase-protection advice is not backed by a citation yet
items.finding: The recommendation to pay by credit card is standard consumer practice but no official CFPB/FTC page was retrieved in this pass to support specific dispute rights. Treat the payment row on the checklist as advice, not as a verified legal claim.
items.buyer_action: Pay by credit card; the protection comes from your card issuer, not from the retailer.

items.title: Spot gold is a single commercial reading, and the page disagreed with itself by $1.08
items.finding: The recorded spot ($4,026.79/oz at 2026-10-22 07:07 NY) is from a commercial aggregator, not an exchange feed. A second ticker on the same page showed $4,025.71. The calculator therefore treats spot as an editable input and stamps every result with the number used.
items.buyer_action: Take the gold price as a reference, not a quote. Two publishers can differ by a dollar.

items.title: Brilliant Earth 18K ring uses 14K white gold prongs
items.finding: The product detail lists “Prong metal: 14K White Gold” on an 18K yellow gold ring. This is a mixed-metal construction, not an error, but it means not all metal in the ring is 18K.
items.buyer_action: If the two-tone detail matters, confirm the karat of every component (band and prongs) in writing.

items.title: Retailers named but not vetted in this pass
items.finding: Costco, James Allen, Tiffany & Co., Aurate and Derco Diamonds appeared during source discovery but were not vetted. No price for them is recorded anywhere in this dataset. Listing them here prevents anyone from mistaking absence for a negative finding.
items.buyer_action: Vet each retailer yourself: phone number, postal address and a live support channel.

items.title: Prices moved between research passes — two rows corrected
items.finding: Re-reading the same two product pages on 2026-10-22 gave different prices from the earlier pass. rs-571223 now lists $849.00 on every in-stock size, so the stored $799.00 floor is no longer on the page. rs-943668 is now a clearance item at $1,269.00 with an original price of $1,795.00, and sizes 5, 6 and 6.5 are sold out; the stored $1,439.00 ceiling was a size variant that is no longer listed. Both rows were corrected to the price the page shows, and the old values are kept in data/reverification.json so nothing is silently overwritten.
items.buyer_action: Treat every price here as a snapshot. Open the product link on the row before you buy, and expect the other 35 rows to have moved too — they were not re-read in this pass.

items.title: Ross-Simons publishes a gold weight on its product pages, but 13 of its 17 rows still have none
items.finding: Ross-Simons renders a "Gold Weight" line in the spec panel of its product pages (for example "Gold Weight 1.7 grams" on item 571221 and "Gold Weight 0.5 grams" on items 981367 and 907250). The earlier passes captured prices and karats but not that field, which is why only 5 of 43 rows carry a weight. Four Ross-Simons rows were filled in pass P12 by re-reading the page; the remaining 13 were not re-read, so their weight stays blank rather than being inferred from a sibling item.
items.buyer_action: If a Ross-Simons row matters to you, open its page and read the Gold Weight line yourself — it is usually there. Send it to me and it can be verified into the table.

items.title: Mejuri's return promise has an exclusion that matters for rings: engraving
items.affected: all Mejuri rows (mej-2mm, mej-db, mej-deb, mej-bde)
items.finding: The Mejuri product page states "We offer free 30-day returns & exchanges starting from the day the shipment is delivered or picked up in-store. Some exclusions apply" and, separately, "Engraved items are not eligible for return." Engraving is offered as an option in the same buy box as the ring, so a personalised ring can lose its return right at checkout.
items.buyer_action: Do not add engraving until you have weighed and inspected the ring, or accept that the purchase becomes final.

items.title: Seller-published weights are approximate — so every melt figure here inherits that error
items.affected: all rows with a published weight (5 of 43)
items.finding: Every Ross-Simons page that shows a weight also states: "All weights and measurements are approximate." A 0.5 g ring priced against gold at 129.56 USD/gram therefore has a melt value with a real tolerance around it, not an exact figure. The site labels those numbers as computed from the published weight and never presents them as an appraisal.
items.buyer_action: Use the melt multiple as an order-of-magnitude check, not to the cent. Have the ring weighed on a jeweller's scale on arrival.

items.title: Mejuri's solid white gold is rhodium-plated on the surface — yellow gold is not
items.affected: Mejuri white-gold variants of the listed rows (the rows themselves are yellow gold)
items.finding: The Mejuri materials panel says: "14k solid white gold pieces are finished with rhodium plating, giving them their signature color along with added shine and durability." That is a surface finish on a solid 14k white gold ring, not a gold substitute — but a buyer filtering for "no plating" should know the white version carries a plating layer that wears over time and is re-polished by jewellers.
items.buyer_action: If plating is a hard no, choose the yellow or rose variants; if you want white, ask the jeweller about re-rhodium cost and interval.
